Let me think through this season carefully. I'll reason in my own voice first, then lay out the plan.

---

**My thinking for this year**

I've been working this land for 30 years — I came to this village when I married, and I've farmed through drought years, bollworm years, good years and bad. My husband works at a construction site in the county town most of the year, so it's mostly me out here now. My son is grown and sends money sometimes but he doesn't come back for farm work. So when I plan the year, I have to think about what my body can handle and what I can hire out.

I've got 9.5 mu split into a few plots. About 6 mu are in cotton — that's what this side of Quzhou has always done, the land suits it, and I know cotton better than anything else. The other 3.5 mu I keep in the wheat-maize rotation. That's mostly for our own grain — we eat the flour, I sell a bit of maize, and it gives me something in the ground year-round instead of bare soil.

**Cotton (6 mu).** I'll plant around April 20th, same as usual. I'll buy Bt cotton seed from the agri-supply shop in town — the village head said the variety we used last year did fine, so I'll stick with it. Changing seed is risky when you don't know how it'll do. Before planting I'll put down compound fertilizer as base — about 40 kg of the 15-15-15 per mu — and then topdress urea at the budding stage, maybe 15 kg. That's roughly 14 kg of pure N per mu altogether. Less than what the extension poster says, but that's what I can afford, and my cotton always comes in around 250 kg lint per mu, which is about what the neighbors get too. I'll irrigate twice from the well — once if April is dry for emergence, and once at peak bloom. Any more and the electricity bill eats the profit. Bollworm has been less of a problem since Bt, but I still spray insecticide two or three times for aphids and mirid bugs. The hard part is picking in September-October — that's when I hire two women from the village to help me, because my back can't take two months of stooping anymore. That labor cost is the biggest line on my cotton.

**Wheat (3.5 mu).** Already planted last October, so this spring I just manage it. I put down compound fertilizer at planting — same 15-15-15 mix, about 35 kg/mu — and I'll topdress urea at jointing in early March, around 12 kg. So about 16 kg N/mu total, which is about right for my yield. I'll irrigate three times: I already did the pre-winter one, then one at jointing and one at grain filling. If spring rain is good I'll skip one and save the pump cost. I'll spray herbicide once for the broadleaf weeds, which I do every year because hand weeding on 3.5 mu is too much. Harvest is early-mid June — I hire the combine from the village cooperative, costs about 50 yuan/mu. Expecting maybe 420 kg/mu, similar to last year.

**Maize (3.5 mu).** Goes in the ground as soon as the wheat combine is off the field — usually June 15th, tight window. I use a hybrid seed, the Zhengdan variety my neighbor swears by. Direct seed into the wheat stubble, no tillage, save time and fuel. I put the starter fertilizer down with the planter and topdress urea at the large bell stage in late July — about 14 kg N/mu total. If July-August is dry I'll irrigate once, otherwise the summer rain does it. No pesticide usually unless I see armyworm, which I haven't the last few years. Harvest late September with a hired combine. Expect about 450 kg/mu.

My total cash outlay will be around 4,800-5,000 yuan. That's what I can budget. I always keep a few hundred yuan aside in case something goes wrong — a pump breaks, or pests hit.
